summary: AI coding tools like Claude Code and Codex produce code with security weaknesses

caption:
Can AI-generated code be trusted? 29.6% of AI-generated code has security flaws

AI coding tools have changed how software gets written, but they've also introduced security risks. A study found 29.6% of AI-generated code snippets contain security weaknesses across 38 CWE categories.

Veracode's 2025 GenAI Code Security Report tested code generated by over 100 LLMs and found a pattern of AI tools writing functional code that disproportionately fails basic security checks.

To mitigate risks, developers can implement checkpoints between AI-generated code and production, including explicit security requirements, fast local checks, and CI/CD catches.

headline_marked: Plex users consider [[Jellyfin as alternative]] after Plex's $750 lifetime pass
headline: Plex users consider Jellyfin as alternative after Plex's $750 lifetime pass
summary: Plex's recent price hike sparks interest in free, open-source alternative Jellyfin
details: Plex's recent price hike from $250 to $750 for a lifetime pass has left some users frustrated. The company's focus on adding features over improving the user interface has also contributed to the discontent.

Jellyfin, a free and open-source media server, offers many of Plex's features, including the ability to stream a personal collection of TV shows and movies. However, it requires more technical setup, especially for remote access.
Jellyfin supports local media streaming on various platforms, but remote access requires users to set up their own networking infrastructure, which may be a barrier for some users.

The article concludes that Jellyfin is a viable alternative for users who primarily want to stream their digital collection within their home network, but may not be suitable for those who rely on remote access or specific features like Live TV and DVR.
